feedback.worked_solution:
Our function consists of two radical functions, so it is continuous over all points in its domain.

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{4-3x}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-3x\ge 0\,⟹\,3x\le 4\,⟹\,x\le \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{x+3}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3\ge 0\,⟹\,x\ge -3\end{aligned}
$$

The domain of $f(x)$ is given by the intersection of the domain of our radical functions:

$$
(-\infty ,\frac{4}{3}]\cap [-3,\infty )=[\,-3,\frac{4}{3}]
$$

and the function is continuous on this interval.
